review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

19:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, μετῆρεν ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.
19:1.targetText: When Jesus had finished saying these things, He left Galilee and went into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

groups.note: BSB renders τοὺς λόγους ("the words") as "saying ... things".
μετῆρεν ἀπό ("departed from") is rendered by the transitive verb "left".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:2.sourceText: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ.
19:2.targetText: Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the opening καί.

19:3.sourceText: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Φαρισαῖοι πειράζοντες αὐτὸν καὶ λέγοντες Εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀπολῦσαι τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ κατὰ πᾶσαν αἰτίαν;
19:3.targetText: Then some Pharisees came and tested Him by asking, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to Him") implicit after "came".
BSB subordinates the saying participle ("by asking") instead of joining it with "and".
Εἰ introduces a direct question here and has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins "came" to the participle πειράζοντες ("testing"), which it renders as the finite verb "tested".
English supplies the subject implied by αὐτοῦ ("his"); some editions read ἀνθρώπῳ ("for a man"), which N1904 lacks.

19:4.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι ὁ κτίσας ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτοὺς
19:4.targetText: Jesus answered, “Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he", which BSB names as Jesus.
ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

19:5.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν Ἕνεκα τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ κολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν;
19:5.targetText: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?

groups.note: ἕνεκα ("on account of") is rendered "For ... reason" around τούτου ("this").
The article τόν has possessive force here.
ἔσονται εἰς ("will be into") is a Semitic idiom for "will become".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:6.sourceText: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ σὰρξ μία. ὃ οὖν ὁ Θεὸς συνέζευξεν, ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.
19:6.targetText: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”

groups.note: The third-person imperative χωριζέτω is rendered "let ... separate".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:7.sourceText: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Τί οὖν Μωϋσῆς ἐνετείλατο δοῦναι βιβλίον ἀποστασίου καὶ ἀπολῦσαι;
19:7.targetText: “Why then,” they asked, “did Moses order a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to Him") implicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the unstated subject of the infinitives "to give" and "send away".
English supplies the unstated recipient of the certificate.
English supplies the object of ἀπολῦσαι; some editions read αὐτήν ("her"), which N1904 lacks.

19:8.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὅτι Μωϋσῆς πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἐπέτρεψεν ὑμῖν ἀπολῦσαι τὰς γυναῖκας ὑμῶν· ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς δὲ οὐ γέγονεν οὕτως.
19:8.targetText: Jesus replied, “Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart; but it was not this way from the beginning.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") implicit.
Ὅτι introduces the direct speech and has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker, who is only the subject of λέγει here.

19:9.sourceText: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην, μοιχᾶται.
19:9.targetText: Now I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman, commits adultery.”

groups.note: μὴ ἐπί ("not on the ground of") is rendered "except for".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:10.sourceText: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί Εἰ οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ αἰτία τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μετὰ τῆς γυναικός, οὐ συμφέρει γαμῆσαι.
19:10.targetText: His disciples said to Him, “If this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.”

groups.note: BSB recasts "the case of the man with (μετά) the wife" as "between ... and".
The article τῆς has possessive force here.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: N1904 has no αὐτοῦ here; BSB's "His" matches the reading οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ found in other editions.

19:11.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐ πάντες χωροῦσιν τὸν λόγον τοῦτον ἀλλ’ οἷς δέδοται.
19:11.targetText: “Not everyone can accept this word,” He replied, “but only those to whom it has been given.

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he".
The relative οἷς includes its unexpressed antecedent ("those to whom").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ or αὐτοῖς ("to them") here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds "only" to sharpen the contrast with "not everyone".

19:12.sourceText: εἰσὶν γὰρ εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνουχίσθησαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνούχισαν ἑαυτοὺς διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν. ὁ δυνάμενος χωρεῖν χωρείτω.
19:12.targetText: For there are eunuchs who were born that way; others were made that way by men; and still others live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.”

groups.note: BSB compresses "there are eunuchs who" to "others".
εὐνουχίσθησαν ("were made eunuchs") is rendered "were made that way".
BSB compresses "there are eunuchs who" to "still others".
BSB renders εὐνούχισαν ἑαυτούς ("made themselves eunuchs") as "live like eunuchs".
The third-person imperative χωρείτω ("let him accept") is rendered "should accept".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός ("from the mother's womb") implicit in "born".
BSB uses a semicolon instead of "and" here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "accept"; χωρεῖν has none.
English supplies the object of "should accept".

19:13.sourceText: Τότε προσηνέχθησαν αὐτῷ παιδία, ἵνα τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιθῇ αὐτοῖς καὶ προσεύξηται· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς.
19:13.targetText: Then the little children were brought to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them and pray for them. And the disciples rebuked those who brought them.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for αὐτῷ ("to him").
The article τάς has possessive force here.
BSB identifies αὐτοῖς ("them") as the people who brought the children.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the children definite; παιδία has no article.
English supplies the people prayed for; προσεύξηται has no object.
English adds this clause to make clear whom the disciples rebuked.

19:14.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτὰ ἐλθεῖν πρός με· τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
19:14.targetText: But Jesus said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:15.sourceText: καὶ ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἐπορεύθη ἐκεῖθεν.
19:15.targetText: And after He had placed His hands on them, He went on from there.

19:16.sourceText: Καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ εἶπεν Διδάσκαλε, τί ἀγαθὸν ποιήσω ἵνα σχῶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον;
19:16.targetText: Just then a man came up to Jesus and inquired, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?”

groups.note: Καὶ ἰδού ("and behold") is rendered "Just then".
εἷς ("one") serves as the indefinite "a man".
BSB names Jesus for αὐτῷ ("to him").

unmappedTarget.reason: English renders the participle προσελθών ("having come up") as "came up" and joins it to "inquired" with "and".

19:17.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τί με ἐρωτᾷς περὶ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ; εἷς ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαθός· εἰ δὲ θέλεις εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν, τήρει τὰς ἐντολάς.
19:17.targetText: “Why do you ask Me about what is good?” Jesus replied. “There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he", which BSB names as Jesus.
τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ("the good") is rendered as the clause "what is good".
ὁ ἀγαθός ("the good one") is rendered as the clause "who is good".
English transitive "enter" absorbs εἰς ("into").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula of the clause "what is good".
English supplies the copula of the clause "who is good".

19:18.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ Ποίας; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔφη Τὸ Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐ ψευδομαρτυρήσεις,
19:18.targetText: “Which ones?” the man asked.  Jesus answered, “‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness,

groups.note: A future with οὐ ("you shall not murder") is a prohibition, rendered "Do not murder".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render δέ here.
The neuter article Τό introduces the quoted commandments; BSB marks them with quotation marks only.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker, who is only the subject of λέγει here.

19:19.sourceText: Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καὶ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
19:19.targetText: honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.’”

groups.note: The article τόν has possessive force here.
The future Ἀγαπήσεις ("you shall love") is a command, rendered "love".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:20.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ νεανίσκος Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφύλαξα· τί ἔτι ὑστερῶ;
19:20.targetText: “All these I have kept,” said the young man. “What do I still lack?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit.

19:21.sourceText: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, ὕπαγε πώλησόν σου τὰ ὑπάρχοντα καὶ δὸς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
19:21.targetText: Jesus told him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

groups.note: The dative plural πτωχοῖς ("to poor people") is rendered "to the poor".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

19:22.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ νεανίσκος τὸν λόγον ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος· ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.
19:22.targetText: When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered as the clause "When ... heard".
τὸν λόγον ("the word") is rendered by the pronoun "this".
The periphrastic ἦν ... ἔχων ("he was having") is rendered "he had".
κτήματα πολλά ("many possessions") is rendered "great wealth".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

19:23.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πλούσιος δυσκόλως εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
19:23.targetText: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.

groups.note: The adverb δυσκόλως ("with difficulty") is recast as "it is hard for".
English transitive "enter" absorbs εἰς ("into"); the future "will enter" is recast as an infinitive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ὅτι, which introduces the quoted statement.

19:24.sourceText: πάλιν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρήματος ῥαφίδος εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
19:24.targetText: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

groups.note: τρῆμα ("hole") is rendered by the English idiom "the eye" of a needle.
N1904's one εἰσελθεῖν ("to enter") serves both clauses; other editions read διελθεῖν ("to pass") for the camel and repeat εἰσελθεῖν for the rich man.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
English transitive "enter" absorbs εἰς ("into").

19:25.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο σφόδρα λέγοντες Τίς ἄρα δύναται σωθῆναι;
19:25.targetText: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, “Who then can be saved?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "heard".
English renders the participle λέγοντες ("saying") as a second finite verb joined by "and".

19:26.sourceText: ἐμβλέψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις τοῦτο ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν, παρὰ δὲ Θεῷ πάντα δυνατά.
19:26.targetText: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

groups.note: BSB makes αὐτοῖς ("to them") the object of "looked at" instead of placing it after "said".
The one ἐστιν is understood again in the second clause, which BSB renders "are".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render this δέ.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English renders the participle ἐμβλέψας ("having looked") as a finite verb joined by "and".

19:27.sourceText: Τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι· τί ἄρα ἔσται ἡμῖν;
19:27.targetText: “Look,” Peter replied, “we have left everything to follow You. What then will there be for us?”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς ... εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.
BSB recasts the aorist ἠκολουθήσαμεν ("we followed") as the purpose "to follow".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render Τότε ("then") here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit.
BSB recasts "and followed" as a purpose clause, so καί has no English counterpart.

19:28.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὑμεῖς οἱ ἀκολουθήσαντές μοι, ἐν τῇ παλινγενεσίᾳ, ὅταν καθίσῃ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ, καθήσεσθε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐπὶ δώδεκα θρόνους κρίνοντες τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
19:28.targetText: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

groups.note: BSB renders the single noun παλινγενεσία ("regeneration") as "renewal of all things".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render δέ here.
BSB does not render ὅτι, which introduces the quoted statement.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The intensive αὐτοί ("you yourselves") repeats the subject and is not rendered separately.

19:29.sourceText: καὶ πᾶς ὅστις ἀφῆκεν οἰκίας ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἐμοῦ ὀνόματός, πολλαπλασίονα λήμψεται καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσει.
19:29.targetText: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
N1904 reads πολλαπλασίονα ("many times as much"); BSB's "a hundredfold" follows the reading ἑκατονταπλασίονα instead.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows the reading ἢ γυναῖκα ("or wife"), which N1904 lacks.
BSB follows the reading ἑκατονταπλασίονα ("a hundredfold"); N1904 has πολλαπλασίονα ("many times as much").

19:30.sourceText: Πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.
19:30.targetText: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.

groups.note: The one ἔσονται is understood again in the second clause, where BSB repeats "will be".

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause for πρῶτοι ("first ones").
